source_title: Yorùbá Òrìṣà Traditions — Ọ̀rúnmìlà-focused Ifá witness
continuity_scope: A deliberately narrow, non-exhaustive witness set about Yorùbá Ifá practice: UNESCO's 2008 Representative List description of the Ifá divination system and the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art's documented Ifá divination-cup label. This is a living sacred tradition, not a closed fictional continuity. It does not merge regional lineages, diaspora traditions in the Americas/Caribbean, individual practitioners, or literary/performative variants.
work_or_witnesses: UNESCO, Ifa divination system, Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, 2008
Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Divination cup, accession 92-10-1, label text
coverage_rule: Include only an individually named being explicitly identified as an individual figure by both selected authoritative witnesses: Ọ̀rúnmìlà (also rendered Orunmila in English-language institutional material). Do not create nodes for Òrìṣà as a category, Ifá as a system/corpus, babaláwo, devotees, offices, signs, odù, ẹsẹ̀, ritual objects, forces, towns, peoples, or unnamed/collective beings. No kinship or other relationships are inferred.
omissions: The quarantined earlier draft at research/batch_006/yoruba_ifa and its QUARANTINED.md are deliberately untouched and remain excluded from compilation; this pass is a separate replacement witness, not an overwrite.

No specific published Ifá verse/oríkì text is asserted in this pass. The witnesses identify the corpus and its performance/transmission but do not support a wider roster of named figures or verse-specific acts.

Òrìṣà categories, Ifá as system/corpus, babaláwo, devotees, odù, ẹsẹ̀, palm nuts, divination chain, ọ̀pọn Ifá, ìròkè Ifá, agere Ifá, shrines, towns, peoples, and diaspora traditions are terms/contexts rather than nodes.
No moral alignment, game class/race, fixed pantheon hierarchy, universal genealogy, equivalence to 'god,' or cross-diaspora identity merge is made.

The witnesses note colonial rule and religious pressures that discriminated against traditional practices. This pass records that safeguarding context without treating it as a complete history of colonialism, slavery, collecting, or all Yorùbá/diaspora experience.
uncertainties: UNESCO writes 'Ifa or Orunmila' for a mystical figure, while also using Ifá for the divination system/corpus. This pass keeps the individual being, system, and corpus visibly distinct rather than treating the terms as interchangeable.

Yorùbá spelling, tonal marks, transliteration, and English archival forms vary by witness. The canonical display form here is Ọ̀rúnmìlà; unmarked 'Orunmila' is retained only as a witness-specific alias, not as a replacement.

The museum label documents an object and its interpretive context, not a complete account of living ritual or object provenance. It is used only for the cited terminology and is not treated as authority over practitioners.
No relationship is added because the selected witnesses do not directly support a character-to-character relation at the required level.
evidence_basis: UNESCO safeguarding documentation and Smithsonian National Museum of African Art object-label documentation only. These institutional descriptions are used as a bounded orientation/reference pass, not as a substitute for lineage-held knowledge, complete Ifá textual witnesses, or living-practitioner authority.
